title: Neighbor Discovery for IP version 6 (IPv6)
subtitle: How IPv6 nodes find routers, resolve neighbors’ link addresses and notice when a neighbor goes quiet.
summary: Neighbor Discovery (ND) is the protocol IPv6 nodes use to talk to the other nodes on the same link. It lets a host find routers, learn which prefixes are on-link, turn a neighbor’s IPv6 address into a link-layer address, and keep checking that a neighbor is still reachable. It does the work that ARP, ICMP Router Discovery and ICMP Redirect did in IPv4, using five ICMPv6 message types.

eli5.summary: When you move into a new street you need to find the mail carrier and learn which house belongs to which neighbor. IPv6 computers shout a quick question on the street, the right one answers, and they keep a little address book and double-check it from time to time.

questions: what is the ndp neighbor cache
how does ipv6 find the default gateway
why must ndp packets have hop limit 255

tldr.problem: An IPv6 node on a link needs to find routers, learn what is on-link, map neighbors’ IPv6 addresses to link-layer addresses and notice when a neighbor stops responding.
tldr.mechanism: It exchanges five ICMPv6 messages (Router Solicitation/Advertisement, Neighbor Solicitation/Advertisement, Redirect) with Hop Limit 255, and keeps a Neighbor Cache whose entries move through INCOMPLETE, REACHABLE, STALE, DELAY and PROBE.
tldr.outcome: It is the link-local control plane of every IPv6 network, and the base for stateless address autoconfiguration, duplicate address detection and later extensions such as SEND.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Neighbor Discovery for IPv6 is the protocol that nodes on the same link use to find each other. The RFC groups the problems it solves as router discovery, prefix discovery, parameter discovery, address autoconfiguration support, address resolution, next-hop determination, neighbor unreachability detection, duplicate address detection and redirect.

In IPv4 these jobs were spread across several protocols. The RFC says Neighbor Discovery “corresponds to a combination of the IPv4 protocols Address Resolution Protocol, ICMP Router Discovery, and ICMP Redirect”, and adds a Neighbor Unreachability Detection algorithm; in IPv4 there is no generally agreed mechanism for it. See RFC 826 for ARP.

Everything runs on top of ICMPv6 (RFC 4443) and the IPv6 addressing rules in RFC 4291. This document obsoletes RFC 2461, and it has since been updated by twelve later RFCs.

Stateless address autoconfiguration itself is specified separately in RFC 4862. Neighbor Discovery supplies the messages and prefixes it relies on.
sections.eli5: When you arrive at a new school you have to find the teacher, learn who sits where and check that your friends are still in their seats. IPv6 computers do all of that with one set of little questions and answers called Neighbor Discovery.

sections.title: The Five Message Types
sections.content:
Neighbor Discovery defines “five different ICMP packet types”: a Router Solicitation and Router Advertisement pair, a Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement pair, and Redirect. Their ICMPv6 type numbers are 133 to 137.

Hosts send Router Solicitations to ask routers to advertise right away. Routers send Router Advertisements periodically, or in reply, carrying prefixes, a suggested hop limit and other link parameters. A node sends a Neighbor Solicitation to learn a neighbor’s link-layer address or to check that the neighbor is still reachable, and the answer is a Neighbor Advertisement. A router sends a Redirect to tell a host about a better first hop.

All five are sent with an IP Hop Limit of 255, and each can carry options (type-length-value records) after the fixed header. Receivers must silently ignore options they do not recognise, which is what lets later RFCs add new ones.

The ICMPv6 type values for these messages and the five option types are listed in the RFC’s IANA section. The document itself needed no new allocations.
sections.eli5: There are five kinds of notes. Two are “is there a teacher?” and “I’m the teacher”. Two are “who sits at this desk?” and “it’s me”. The last is the teacher saying “talk to that person instead, it’s quicker”.

sections.title: Message and Option Formats
sections.content:
Every Neighbor Discovery message begins with the ICMPv6 header: an 8-bit Type, an 8-bit Code (always 0) and a 16-bit Checksum. After that, each message has its own fixed fields and then a list of options.

A Neighbor Solicitation (type 135) has 32 reserved bits and a 128-bit Target Address, which must not be a multicast address. A Neighbor Advertisement (type 136) starts with three flags: R (sender is a router), S (sent in answer to a solicitation) and O (override the cached link-layer address). Its remaining 29 bits are reserved. The Router Advertisement (type 134) carries Cur Hop Limit, the M and O flags (use DHCPv6 for addresses, or for other configuration), a 16-bit Router Lifetime in seconds, Reachable Time and Retrans Timer in milliseconds.

Options 1 and 2
Source and Target Link-Layer Address. Length is counted in units of 8 octets, so it is 1 for IEEE 802 addresses.
Option 3
Prefix Information: Type 3, Length 4, prefix length, an L (on-link) flag, an A (autonomous configuration) flag, Valid and Preferred Lifetimes and a 128-bit prefix.
Options 4 and 5
Redirected Header (as much of the original packet as fits in the minimum IPv6 MTU) and MTU (a recommended link MTU).
sections.eli5: Every note starts with the same label on the envelope saying what kind of note it is. Inside there are a few boxes to tick, like “I am a teacher”, and then room for extra stickers such as “here is my desk number”.

sections.title: Router and Prefix Discovery
sections.content:
When an interface comes up, a host waits a random delay of up to MAX_RTR_SOLICITATION_DELAY (1 second) and then sends a Router Solicitation, normally to the all-routers multicast address FF02::2. If no advertisement arrives it retries every RTR_SOLICITATION_INTERVAL (4 seconds), up to MAX_RTR_SOLICITATIONS (3) times.

Routers answer with a Router Advertisement from their link-local address, to the soliciting host or to the all-nodes address FF02::1. Hosts use the advertisement in three ways. The Router Lifetime puts the router on a Default Router List (a lifetime of zero means it is not a default router). Prefix Information options tell the host which prefixes are on-link (L flag) and which may be used to build addresses automatically (A flag). The Cur Hop Limit, Reachable Time, Retrans Timer and MTU values become link parameters.

A destination covered by no advertised prefix is, by default, reached through a router. A Redirect can later tell the host that the destination is actually a neighbor.

The M and O flags do not assign addresses. They only tell hosts whether DHCPv6 is available for addresses or for other configuration such as DNS servers.
sections.eli5: A new kid says “is there a grown-up here?” and the grown-up shouts back where the exits are, which street names count as “our neighborhood” and how loud to talk. Now the kid knows who to ask for help getting to places farther away.

sections.title: Address Resolution
sections.content:
Address resolution is IPv6’s replacement for ARP. A node that has a packet for an on-link neighbor but no link-layer address creates a Neighbor Cache entry in the INCOMPLETE state and sends a Neighbor Solicitation. The solicitation goes not to everyone but to the solicited-node multicast address for the target, a link-local multicast address computed from the target address (the function is in RFC 4291). Only nodes whose addresses map to that group have to look at it.

The solicitation includes the sender’s own link-layer address as a Source Link-Layer Address option, so the target can reply by unicast with a Neighbor Advertisement carrying its Target Link-Layer Address. “A single request-response pair of packets is sufficient for both the initiator and the target to resolve each other’s link-layer addresses.”

While waiting, the sender queues packets for the neighbor and retransmits about every RetransTimer (1,000 ms by default). After MAX_MULTICAST_SOLICIT (3) tries without an answer, resolution fails and queued packets are answered with ICMP Destination Unreachable, code 3 (Address Unreachable). The same solicitation, sent from the unspecified address, is what Duplicate Address Detection uses.

Unsolicited Neighbor Advertisements announce a link-layer address change, but the RFC calls them “a performance enhancement only”. Neighbor Unreachability Detection ensures the new address is found reliably anyway.
sections.eli5: To find who lives at a house, you do not shout to the whole town. You call out to a small group of houses whose numbers end the same way. The right person writes their door number on a card and hands it back, and you keep it in your address book.

sections.title: Neighbor Unreachability Detection
sections.content:
A cached link-layer address can go stale: the neighbor may crash, move or lose its path. Neighbor Unreachability Detection (NUD) checks whether packets sent to a neighbor are really being processed there. It only runs for neighbors the node is actually sending to, so an idle neighbor costs no traffic.

Positive confirmation comes from two sources: a solicited Neighbor Advertisement, or a “hint” from an upper-layer protocol such as TCP that new acknowledgments are arriving. A Neighbor Cache entry is in one of five states: INCOMPLETE, REACHABLE, STALE, DELAY or PROBE. After ReachableTime milliseconds without confirmation an entry becomes STALE. The next packet sent moves it to DELAY, which waits DELAY_FIRST_PROBE_TIME (5 seconds) for an upper-layer hint. Without one the node enters PROBE and sends unicast solicitations every RetransTimer until it gets an answer. After MAX_UNICAST_SOLICIT (3) unanswered probes the entry is deleted.

For neighbors that are default routers, failure triggers next-hop determination again, so a host can switch to another router. ReachableTime is a random value derived from the base value, between 0.5 and 1.5 times it (MIN_RANDOM_FACTOR and MAX_RANDOM_FACTOR), with a default base of 30,000 ms.
sections.eli5: You keep your friend’s phone number in your book. If you have not talked in a while, you do not call at once. You wait until you need them, and if your game of catch shows they are still there, you are done. If not, you call a few times, and if nobody answers you cross them out.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC is blunt that Neighbor Discovery “is subject to attacks that cause IP packets to flow to unexpected places”. It groups the main threats into denial of service, address spoofing and router spoofing. For example, a forged Router Advertisement can make hosts drop every legitimate default router and on-link prefix, or make an attacker the default router.

Without authentication, the protocol’s main defense is the Hop Limit rule. Every received ND packet must have a Hop Limit of 255. Because routers decrement the Hop Limit on forwarded packets, a packet that arrives with 255 must have been sent by a neighbor on the same link, so off-link senders are ignored.

That does not stop a malicious node on the same link. Cryptographic protection is out of scope here and is defined in SEcure Neighbor Discovery (SEND, RFC 3971). The RFC also notes that IPsec can be used, but that IKE is not suited to setting up the dynamic security associations needed for address resolution.

The 255 check protects against remote attackers only. Any host on the link can still spoof Neighbor and Router Advertisements unless SEND or a switch-level defence is in use.
sections.eli5: Someone could pretend to be the grown-up or the friend you are looking for. The rule is that you only trust notes from someone standing right next to you, because notes from far away have a smudged number on them. But a bully standing next to you can still fib, so there are extra locks you can add.

fields.desc: IPv6 address being resolved or checked. Must not be a multicast address.

fields.desc: Default Hop Limit for outgoing packets. Zero means unspecified.

fields.name: M
fields.desc: Managed address configuration: addresses are available via DHCPv6.

fields.name: O
fields.desc: Other configuration is available via DHCPv6.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Unused. Sender sets to zero, receiver ignores.

fields.name: Router Lifetime
fields.desc: Seconds the router may be used as a default router. Zero means it is not one.

fields.name: Reachable Time
fields.desc: Milliseconds a node assumes a neighbor is reachable after confirmation. Zero means unspecified.

fields.name: Retrans Timer
fields.desc: Milliseconds between retransmitted Neighbor Solicitations. Zero means unspecified.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Option type.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Option length in units of 8 octets.

fields.name: Prefix Length
fields.desc: Number of leading bits in Prefix that are valid, 0 to 128.

fields.name: L
fields.desc: On-link flag: the prefix can be used for on-link determination.

fields.name: A
fields.desc: Autonomous address-configuration flag.

fields.name: Reserved1
fields.desc: Unused. Sender sets to zero.

fields.name: Valid Lifetime
fields.desc: Seconds the prefix is valid for on-link determination. All ones means infinity.

fields.name: Preferred Lifetime
fields.desc: Seconds that addresses generated from the prefix remain preferred. All ones means infinity.

fields.name: Reserved2
fields.desc: Unused. Sender sets to zero.

fields.name: Prefix
fields.desc: An IPv6 address or prefix. Bits after Prefix Length are zero.

viz.caption: Threats and defences in the RFC

items.title: Denial of service
items.text: Forged Router Advertisements can time out every legitimate default router and on-link prefix.

items.title: Address spoofing
items.text: A malicious node can answer solicitations for addresses it does not own and attract traffic.

items.title: Router spoofing
items.text: A node can claim to be a router and become the default route for the link.

items.title: Hop Limit 255
items.text: Receivers drop ND packets with any other Hop Limit, so off-link senders are ignored. SEND (RFC 3971) adds cryptographic protection.

today: Neighbor Discovery runs on essentially every IPv6 network. Every IPv6 host and router implements it, so it is in the Linux, BSD, Windows and macOS stacks. You see it as the neighbor table (ip -6 neigh on Linux, ndp -a on BSD and macOS) and as ICMPv6 types 133–137 in packet captures. Stateless address configuration and Duplicate Address Detection build on it. Many later RFCs update this one, for example RFC 6980, which restricts fragmentation of ND messages.
